title: Sin Is Crouching at the Door

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the Lord said to Cain, "Why are you angry? Why is your face downcast? If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you do not do what is right, sin is crouching at your door; it desires to have you, but you must rule over it." - Gen 4:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before Cain ever raised his hand against his brother, God came to him in mercy. Notice this: God warns before He judges. He questions Cain gently, then paints a vivid picture - sin is like a wild animal crouching at the door, ready to pounce. It "desires to have you," God says, "but you must rule over it."

This is one of the most honest pictures of temptation in all of Scripture. Sin is not a small thing waiting politely. It is crouching, hungry, wanting to master us. And the moment of choice comes before the sin does - in that heavy, angry, downcast feeling that we either surrender to God or nurse in our hearts.

God's words also carry hope. Cain was not helpless. He was told he could rule over it. And on this side of the cross, we have even more - the Spirit of God living in us, giving us power to say no to sin (Rom 8:13).

The door is where the battle is won or lost. Deal with anger, envy and resentment early, at the door, before they walk in and take over.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What sin is crouching at your door right now?
- Are you fighting it at the door, or letting it inside?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for warning me before I fall. By Your Spirit, help me rule over the sin that wants to rule me.
